To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The bioavailability of lead (Pb) in the kidney is mediated in-part by binding to high-affinity cytosolic Pb binding proteins of 11,000 and 63, 000 daltons, which is not found in the liver.
1) Pb inhibits ALAD noncompetitively, 2) the inhibition is more pronounced in liver than in kidney, and 3) the 11.500 dalton protein can partially reverse Pb-inhibition of ALAD activity.

1) renal Pb-binding protein (11.5 kD) protects hepatic delta-aminoleuvulinic acid dehydrotase from Pb inhibition, 2) the protective effect is dependent on the concentration 3) the 11. 5 kD PbBP has a higher affinity for Pb than the 63 kD PbBP, and 4) the 63 kDa PbBP does not protect ALAD from Pb inhibition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the inhibition of delta- amino-levulinic acid dehydrogenase (ALAD; EC 4.2.1.24) by lead in the kidney and liver.
the regulation of delta-aminolaevulinic acid dehydra-tase (ALAD, EC 4.2.1.24) by lead (Pb).
the role of lead (Pb) binding proteins in the regulation of Pb toxicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PbBP in the kidney is a high affinity, low molecular weight, and low capacity protein that is not found in liver, and that the renal PbBP may protect the renal ALAD from Pb inhibition.
PbBP is not the only factor that determines the differential sensitivity of renal and liver ALAD to Pb inhibition.
the 11. 5K PbBP has a high affinity for Pb (Kd = 0.1 microM) and can bind Pb in the absence or presence of ALAD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 11.500 dalton Pb-binding protein is the most important Pb-binding protein in kidney, but it is not the major Pb-binding protein in liver.
the 11. 5K protein is an important factor in the regulation of ALAD activity in the presence of Pb and that the 63K protein is involved in the transport of Pb into the renal cytosol.
we have demonstrated that the kidney is more resistant than liver to lead toxicity.

lead is more toxic to the kidney than the liver.
